key_insight: DeepONet learns the Couette-flow solution operator across slip and wall-velocity conditions, while PINN gives the best single-case accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate model enables near-real-time prediction of wall-slip Couette flow, which is useful for rapid design studies and control-oriented fluid dynamics applications.
method: PINN solves the governing equations for a specific parameter set using physics constraints.
DeepONet is trained on high-fidelity Crank-Nicolson data to generalize across boundary-condition variations.
Both models are benchmarked against numerical solutions for accuracy and inference speed.
evidence_signal: From the abstract, the PINN reached 0.083% relative L2 error, while DeepONet achieved 0.36% mean error on unseen cases and 0.88% on out-of-distribution signals, with about 540× speedup over the solver.
watch_item: DeepONet is fast, but it still depends on representative training data and may degrade when extrapolating beyond the sampled slip and velocity range.
paper_title: Solution of the Newtonian plane Couette flow with dynamic wall slip using machine-learning methods
